item.title: German Reform Plan Could Lift 2027 GDP Above 1%, Merz Tells ARD
item.description: The package of reforms just laid out by Germany’s coalition could lift the nation’s GDP above 1% in 2027, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told ARD.

item.title: Prison Phone Company Aventiv Clears Hurdle for Lenders’ Takeover
item.description: Aventiv Technologies has clinched an out-of court deal for lenders to take control of the prison phone company from private equity firm Platinum Equity, capping a lengthy slog to clear regulatory approval, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Germany Should Stop Shutting Off Coal Plants, Grid Operator Says
item.description: Germany should stop further closures of coal-fed power plants for now to safeguard electricity supplies amid the expansion of renewable generation, grid operator Amprion GmbH urged.

item.title: Tech, Finance Titans Redraw Stablecoin Map in Threat to Circle
item.description: For years, the stablecoin race has been defined by a simple objective: build the dominant digital dollar. This week’s turbulence in Circle Internet Group Inc.’s shares suggests investors are beginning to price a different future — one in which the biggest rewards may accrue not to the companies issuing stablecoins, but to those controlling how they move.

item.title: ECB Made Right Choice on Rate Hike, Lagarde Tells Les Echos
item.description: The European Central Bank was correct to raise interest rates when it did last month, President Christine Lagarde told Les Echos.

item.title: Soybeans Drift as China Buying Awaited After US Tariff Statement
item.description: Soybean futures drifted between small gains and losses as traders weighed a statement by China’s government on rolling back tariffs on US agricultural products, a move that could pave the way for purchases by the Asian country.

item.title: Amazon to Begin Internet Service This Year After Latest Launch
item.description: A United Launch Alliance rocket lofted 29 satellites for Amazon.com Inc., paving the way for the start of the company’s broadband service later this year in a challenge to SpaceX’s dominant Starlink network.

item.title: Fuel Shortages Stall Venezuela Rescue Efforts as Cranes Sit Idle
item.description: Excavators and cranes ground to a halt at some rescue sites in Venezuela as fuel shortages hampered recovery efforts after last week’s earthquake, leaving crews unable to clear debris in some of the hardest-hit areas of La Guaira state.

item.title: JPMorgan Says Saylor’s Strategy Adds New Risk to Bitcoin Market
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. warns that Michael Saylor’s financing overhaul at Strategy Inc. has shaken up the dynamics of the Bitcoin market by introducing the risk that one of the cryptocurrency’s biggest buyers could also become a seller, adding a new source of uncertainty for investors.

item.title: UBS Attacks Swiss Central Bank for ‘Misleading’ Stability Report
item.description: UBS Group AG has criticized the Swiss National Bank for a “misleading” regulatory report on the lender’s readiness for stricter capital rules.

item.title: Chip Stocks Off to Rough Start in Third Quarter With 2-Day Skid
item.description: Semiconductor stocks are starting the third quarter with their worst two-day selloff in nearly a month.

item.title: Jersey Mike’s, Cumberland Farms Join Swelling IPO Pipeline in US
item.description: Blackstone Inc.-backed Jersey Mike’s Subs Inc. and gas-station and convenience-store operator Cumberland Farms Ltd. filed for initial public offerings as the market for new US listings broadens beyond companies powering the artificial intelligence revolution.

item.title: Canada’s Pembina Advances Gas-Fired Data Center Project
item.description: Pembina Pipeline Corp. will move ahead with a project build a C$4.6 billion ($3.2 billion) gas-fired electricity plant that will power a data center project in Alberta.

item.title: DOJ Probes Alleged Insider Trading Scheme That Stung Susquehanna
item.description: The Justice Department is looking into Susquehanna International Group’s allegations that unknown insider traders made $100 million on options bets placed ahead of a recent Chinese regulatory crackdown on cross-border brokerages, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: EG’s Gas-Station Firm Cumberland Farms Files for US IPO
item.description: Cumberland Farms Ltd, the gas station and convenience store operator, filed for a US initial public offering, joining a rush of debuts that’s powered a record start to the year.

item.title: Danish Central Bank Intervenes to Defend Krone Peg After Slide
item.description: Denmark’s central bank propped up the krone through interventions to defend its peg to the euro after the krone weakened to its lowest level against Europe’s common currency in more than 25 years.

item.title: Florida’s Brightline Taps Reserves to Make Key Bond Payments
item.description: Brightline, the debt-laden Florida private railroad, tapped reserves to made a July 1 interest payment due to holders of its senior municipal bonds and corporate notes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: China’s Kling AI Raises $2 Billion to Expand AI Video
item.description: China’s Kling AI has raised an initial $2 billion in venture capital funding as the spinoff from Kuaishou Technology seeks to expand its video AI operations.

item.title: BOE’s Mann Says She Is Ready to Hike if Price Pressures Persist
item.description: Bank of England rate-setter Catherine Mann says she is prepared to make an “activist” hike if inflation expectations and other price warnings do not improve later this year.

item.title: America Runs on Natural Gas: Fuel Set to Surpass Oil as US Top Energy Source by 2030
item.description: For 75 years, petroleum has been the energy source that has powered the US more than any other. That’s about to change.

item.title: Mexico’s Export-Led Economy at Risk With Annual USMCA Reviews
item.description: For years, Mexico’s pitch to investors rested on a simple promise: build here, sell to the US.

item.title: Quantum Computing Firm IQM Falls After Going Public Via SPAC
item.description: IQM shares slipped in their first day of trading after the Finnish quantum computer producer went public in New York via a merger with a black-check firm.

item.title: Seis gráficos que explican el debilitamiento de la economía de China
item.description: Mercado inmobiliario en declive, población a la baja y menos gasto de consumo son algunos de los factores que han debilitado el crecimiento económico de la superpotencia.

item.title: AI Debt Deluge Makes Credit Market Look Safer While Masking Risk
item.description: On paper, the US corporate bond market is getting safer as more high-rated tech companies sell debt. Many investors fear that safety will prove illusory.

item.title: SAS CEO Is Likely Air Canada Boss After Crash Video Debacle
item.description: SAS AB Chief Executive Officer Anko van der Werff is emerging as a frontrunner to lead Air Canada, according to people familiar with the matter, succeeding Michael Rousseau, who said in March he’d leave after a public outcry over the his omission to speak French in a corporate video.

item.title: Chanel Buys Charvet, Maker of $750 Shirts Favored by Churchill
item.description: Chanel agreed to buy Charvet, the oldest shirtmaker in France that once counted Winston Churchill among its clients and whose striped linen shirts typically go for about €655 ($746).

item.title: The German Warship Reversal That Sank a Landmark Tank IPO
item.description: It’s been a rough few weeks for Europe’s ambitious rearmament efforts.

item.title: White House’s Hassett Criticizes Powell for Staying on at Fed
item.description: White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett criticized former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for staying on at the US central bank, a move that’s preventing the administration from putting another pick on the board.

item.title: Anthropic in Talks With Samsung for Custom AI Chip: Information
item.description: Anthropic PBC is in talks with Samsung Electronics Co. to be a manufacturing partner for a custom artificial intelligence chip, the Information said, citing people familiar with the plan.

item.title: Cuba’s Bold Free-Market Turn Fails to Convince US It’s Ready to Change
item.description: Cuba is struggling to convince the Trump administration that its most ambitious economic reforms in decades are enough to spark the changes the US is demanding.
